A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TweedieMix work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and matchable despite the expanded evaluation and reorganized appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation scores, human-preference studies, image and video comparisons, and component ablations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds DINO scores, parameter sensitivity experiments, runtime comparisons, style composition and additional video-model tests.

M1.justification: The two-stage sampling procedure, resampling strategy, regional masks, Tweedie-space fusion and video feature injection remain unchanged. The Stable Video Diffusion experiment explicitly applies the same injection method; the revised transition timestep is an experimental setting change.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds qualitative composition of object-specific styles, including Pixar/Lego and anime/Picasso combinations. The Custom Concept 101 and animated-character data sources remain unchanged. Enlarging the concept sample changes sampling, while four-concept examples overlap v1's already stated coverage of combinations exceeding three concepts.

E2.justification: v2 adds vanilla sampling as the comparator for style composition and adds ConceptWeaver outputs beside examples previously presented only as TweedieMix results in v1 Figure 11, now Figures 14–16. The main Table 1 comparator set and the DreamVideo comparison remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes quantitative evaluation from 15 concepts in five combinations to 32 in ten, retains 100 images per model, and adds DINOv2 similarity. Appendix A revises t_con from 0.2T to 0.8T and its reported stable range from 0.2–0.3T to 0.7–0.8T, without establishing whether this corrects documentation or reflects rerunning experiments. New experiments introduce parameter variations, a timed inference comparison and a second video backbone.

E4.justification: The original component ablations remain, while v2 adds qualitative sensitivity tests for t_con at 0.8T, 0.6T and 0.4T and resampling counts of 0, 2 and 5. It also adds a four-concept scalability case and a with/without-injection comparison on Stable Video Diffusion. Figures 9, 11 and 12 substantially expand analysis of sensitivity, scalability and transfer across backbones.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. Average-score reporting and the user-study participant counts remain unchanged; the larger concept sample is an evaluation-design change.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces all CLIP score pairs under the revised evaluation: TweedieMix changes from 0.3872/0.8202 to 0.3816/0.8311 for text/image similarity. New DINO scores include 0.5950 for TweedieMix and 0.5352 for ConceptWeaver. These are not same-setting performance gains. New sensitivity, runtime, style, four-concept and video-backbone results expand the findings; Table 2 and the human-preference scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 and the DDIM, CFG, CFG++, fusion and feature-interpolation formulations are unchanged. The expanded appendices introduce no new formal assumptions, mathematical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of inference-time multi-concept composition, improved concept fidelity and a training-free video extension. The abstract's added description of residual-feature transfer explains a mechanism already present in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly explains how fewer concept-fusion steps produce more generic appearances, and Appendix C interprets runtime alongside output quality. Appendix D explicitly discusses applicability to distinct styles. The complex-prompt limitation and its attribution to the pretrained backbone are retained, moving from Appendix B to Appendix F.

D1.justification: v2 specifies DINOv2-base and its object-crop embedding comparison, explicitly documents the 15-concept/five-combination ablation setup, and explains which stages are included or excluded in runtime measurements. It also revises the transition-timestep documentation. The project link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds ConceptExpress by Hao et al. to the related-work discussion and DINOv2 by Oquab et al. for evaluation. The principal positioning against weight merging, inversion and attention-manipulation approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose is retained. v2 lightly edits the abstract and other sentences, updates publication headers, adds acknowledgements, and organizes the expanded appendix into separate sensitivity, efficiency, style, additional-results and limitations sections.

P2.justification: The appendix's visual presentation expands substantially with new sensitivity, style, four-concept and Stable Video Diffusion figures. v1 Figure 11 is split and rearranged into three comparisons with ConceptWeaver in v2 Figures 14–16. Table 1 gains a DINO column; the original failure examples and remaining image/video galleries are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's smaller, CLIP-based evaluation, the broader concept sample and added DINO identity scores strengthen support for the central fidelity claim. Sensitivity tests, runtime comparisons and another video backbone make validation more informative. These are useful incremental gains: the new robustness evidence is mostly qualitative, uncertainty reporting remains absent, and the substantial transition-timestep revision is unexplained.
